Greek art commonly identifies him through a thunderbolt, his characteristic weapon and symbol. Museum objects preserve this association across centuries, providing a useful cultural anchor for remembering the name without inventing a Malay root or an unsupported borrowing history. [Zeus in Greek art](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/251078)

etymology.historical_story: The word family behind zombi is associated with Caribbean Creole forms such as zonbi and ultimately with Bantu vocabulary for spirits. International horror storytelling developed the familiar walking-dead image. Malay uses the spelling zombi, which DBP explicitly recommends as the equivalent of English zombie; this does not establish the precise historical route into Malay. [Merriam-Webster: zombie](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/zombie) [DBP: zombi](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=horror)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: zombi 与英语 zombie 形近；想象熬夜后走路机械、脑袋发空的自己，就能记住它的比喻义。

etymology.historical_story: Zarah comes from Arabic dharra, meaning a tiny particle or speck. Malay preserves that smallness in the everyday dust sense and uses the same word for scientific particles. Its Jawi spelling, ذره, also illustrates how an Arabic borrowing can acquire a conventional Malay written form. This connects a familiar image of dust with the less visible world described in physics. [Zarah: etymology](https://ms.wiktionary.org/wiki/zarah)

etymology.historical_story: Zakir corresponds to Arabic dhākir, an active participle meaning one who remembers. In Islamic language, remembrance often concerns God, linking the name semantically with zikir. This Arabic relationship explains the name's meaning; it does not establish a productive Malay derivation or a verified DBP common-noun entry. The participle is described in [a Quranic concordance](https://www.altafsir.com/Books/Concordance_Of_the_Sublime_Quran.pdf).

etymology.historical_story: Zeta belongs to the Greek alphabetic tradition. Its letterform descends from Phoenician zayin, reflecting the wider adaptation of Phoenician writing by Greek communities. In Malay, zeta functions as a borrowed letter name. Learning it therefore connects a modern classroom symbol with a much older history of writing across Mediterranean cultures. [University of Athens: The Greek Alphabet](https://www-old.phil.uoa.gr/fileadmin/phil.uoa.gr/uploads/linguistics/Pdf/papers/Pantelidis_2014_The_Greek_Alphabet___Scriptura_Mundi.pdf)

Its meaning later expanded to energy and zest, allowing a sound-like word to describe lively advertising or an exciting flavour.
